given:
A 640x480 RGB image is open at C:\ds\img.png. SegmentManager holds exactly one segment: class_id 2, class_aliases {2: 'dog'}, whose visible pixels (after any crop and pixel-priority resolution) form ONE connected block covering 0-based columns 100-109 and rows 50-59 inclusive (100 px). The export context is built exactly as in save_export_manager.py:394-431 (identically at save_export_manager.py:488-515, save_worker.py:55-97 and main_window.py:6596-6630):
  - image_size = (pixmap.height(), pixmap.width()) = (480, 640), i.e. (HEIGHT, WIDTH) in that order (save_export_manager.py:397,421; main_window.py:6601). Getting this pair backwards is the single easiest way to break the rewrite.
  - class_order = SegmentManager.get_unique_class_ids() = [2] - the ASCENDING SORTED list of distinct class_id values (segment_manager.py:87-95).
  - class_labels[i] = get_class_alias(class_order[i]) = ['dog'] - the alias if one is registered for that class id, otherwise str(class_id) (segment_manager.py:397-399).
  - instances = [{'class_id': 2, 'channel': 0, 'contours': [the block's single contour]}]. 'channel' is the INDEX of the class inside class_order, not the class id (segment_manager.py:276,283). Contours come from cv2.findContours(RETR_EXTERNAL, CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE) applied to each segment's own mask ANDed with the final tensor channel (segment_manager.py:297-311).
  - mask_tensor is (H, W, C) uint8 with C = len(class_order).
when: PascalVocExporter.export(ctx) runs (pascal_voc.py:22-63) - i.e. the user saves while Pascal VOC is among the selected export formats. Pascal VOC is NOT a default: DEFAULT_EXPORT_FORMATS = {NPZ, YOLO_DETECTION} (exporters/__init__.py:60-63), so this path is only reached when the user explicitly selects it.
then:
The file C:\ds\img.xml is written (path = os.path.splitext(image_path)[0] + '.xml', pascal_voc.py:62-63; the parent directory is created if missing, pascal_voc.py:56) and its exact content is:

<?xml version='1.0' encoding='utf-8'?>
<annotation>
  <filename>img.png</filename>
  <size>
    <width>640</width>
    <height>480</height>
    <depth>3</depth>
  </size>
  <object>
    <name>dog</name>
    <pose>Unspecified</pose>
    <truncated>0</truncated>
    <difficult>0</difficult>
    <bndbox>
      <xmin>100</xmin>
      <ymin>50</ymin>
      <xmax>110</xmax>
      <ymax>60</ymax>
    </bndbox>
  </object>
</annotation>

Byte-level facts that a byte-identical rewrite must reproduce (pascal_voc.py:57-59, which calls ET.indent(tree) then tree.write(path, encoding='unicode', xml_declaration=True)):
  - XML declaration uses SINGLE quotes and lowercase utf-8: <?xml version='1.0' encoding='utf-8'?>
  - indentation is exactly two spaces per level; element order is fixed: filename, size(width, height, depth), then one object per box with children name, pose, truncated, difficult, bndbox(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax).
  - the stream is written in Python text mode, so line separators are the PLATFORM newline: CRLF on Windows, LF on Linux/macOS. Verified on this Windows box - the first bytes are b"<?xml version='1.0' encoding='utf-8'?>\r\n<annotation>\r\n  <filename>img.png</filename>\r\n".
  - there is NO trailing newline: the file ends with b'</annotation>' (verified).
  - encoding is UTF-8; &, < and > inside a class alias are escaped (alias 'a & <b>' is written as 'a & <b>', verified). Quotes are NOT escaped in element text.

Where each number comes from: width 640 and height 480 are w and h from ctx.image_size unpacked as 'h, w' at pascal_voc.py:23 and written at 28-30. depth is the LITERAL string '3', never derived from the image (pascal_voc.py:31). filename is os.path.basename(ctx.image_path), i.e. the bare file name with no directory (pascal_voc.py:26). name is ctx.class_labels[channel] = 'dog' (pascal_voc.py:37,40). pose 'Unspecified', truncated '0' and difficult '0' are literal strings (pascal_voc.py:41-43). cv2.boundingRect on the contour returns (x, y, bw, bh) = (100, 50, 10, 10) - boundingRect's w/h COUNT BOTH EDGE PIXELS - and the exporter writes xmin=x=100, ymin=y=50, xmax=x+bw=110, ymax=y+bh=60 (pascal_voc.py:36,46-49). So coordinates are 0-BASED and xmax/ymax are EXCLUSIVE: xmax-xmin is the pixel width.
and:
File-level behaviour, and the import side the same rule must pin down (the writer and reader are one contract; changing either alone corrupts every save/load cycle):
  (1) If iter_object_contours yields nothing, export returns None, NO file is written, and an existing img.xml is left untouched (pascal_voc.py:33,50,52-53). export_all never deletes anything (exporters/__init__.py:189-206). Old sidecars are only removed when the image has zero segments at all, via a separate delete path (save_export_manager.py:106-109).
  (2) Reload precondition: FileManager.load_existing_mask walks _LOAD_CHAIN = (.npz, _seg.txt, _coco.json, _CM.npz, .xml, _createml.json, .txt) and reads the FIRST that exists (file_manager.py:128-136,173-205). The VOC file is only read when no .npz, _seg.txt, _coco.json or _CM.npz sits next to the image - which, given NPZ is a default export format, is often not the case.
  (3) Round-trip for the worked example, VERIFIED by executing the legacy code: navigating to an image calls SegmentManager.clear(), which WIPES class_aliases (segment_manager.py:20-26, called from file_navigation_manager.py:281 and main_window.py:2141). load_pascal_voc_xml then parses one object, label 'dog', box (100, 50, 110, 60) (file_manager.py:472-490), and _add_box_segments clamps it and fills mask[50:60, 100:110] (file_manager.py:394-401). Result: exactly ONE segment {'mask': bool (480,640) True over rows 50-59 and cols 100-109 = 100 px, 'type': 'Loaded', 'vertices': None, 'class_id': 0} and class_aliases == {0: 'dog'}. The PIXELS round-trip exactly; the CLASS ID DOES NOT - class 2 comes back as class 0. The alias text survives, the numeric id does not.
  (4) Label -> class id resolution (_build_label_map, file_manager.py:345-379), in this order for the whole file at once: a label equal to an existing alias takes that alias's id; else a label that parses as a Python int takes that integer as its id; else the label is queued and, ONLY AFTER every numeric label has claimed its id, assigned the LOWEST FREE id and registered as a new alias. The two-pass ordering is deliberate: it stops a file mixing 'dog' with '0' from merging both into class 0 (test_bbox_roundtrip.py:525-547).
  (5) _build_label_map is fed EVERY parsed label BEFORE any box is clamped or dropped (file_manager.py:392). A label whose box is later discarded still consumes a class id and still registers an alias. Verified: an XML whose objects are ['' -> '0', 'dog' (box collapses), 'cat', 'fox'] yields segments for class 0, 2 and 3 only, yet class_aliases == {1: 'dog', 2: 'cat', 3: 'fox'} - id 1 is burned by an object that produced nothing.
parameters: Hard-coded constants in the writer (pascal_voc.py): depth = '3' (line 31), pose = 'Unspecified' (41), truncated = '0' (42), difficult = '0' (43), output suffix '.xml' (63). Serialization constants (57-59): two-space indent, XML declaration <?xml version='1.0' encoding='utf-8'?> with single quotes, UTF-8, platform newline (CRLF on Windows), no trailing newline. Coordinate convention: 0-based pixel indices, xmin/ymin inclusive, xmax/ymax EXCLUSIVE, so width = xmax - xmin and height = ymax - ymin. image_size is (height, width). Loader constants (file_manager.py): missing <name> text -> '0' (482); missing bndbox child -> '0' (483-486); coordinate conversion int(round(float(text))) using Python banker's rounding (halves to even); clamp to [0, w] x [0, h] (395-396); drop when x2 <= x1 or y2 <= y1 (397-398); loaded segments get type 'Loaded' and vertices None (406-407). The card's 'parameters' was missing pose/truncated/difficult and every serialization and loader constant.
edgeCases: depth is the literal '3' for EVERY image - grayscale, RGBA, 16-bit, anything (pascal_voc.py:31). It is never read back on import, so it is cosmetically wrong but behaviourally inert. Reproduce it as-is.

<size> is written but IGNORED on import (file_manager.py:456-493 never reads it). The image size used to rebuild masks is the real image's, passed in by load_existing_mask (file_manager.py:178-185). Boxes are never rescaled to match a stale <size>.
pose, truncated and difficult are written and never read back. No import path parses them.

One <object> per CONTOUR, not per segment (pascal_voc.py:35 -> exporters/__init__.py:114-136). A segment made of two disconnected blobs writes TWO objects. Order is: segment order in ctx.instances, then OpenCV contour order within each segment. Confirmed by test_bbox_roundtrip.py:256-268 (two segments of the same class -> two <object> elements).

When ctx.instances is EMPTY the exporter falls back to contouring the merged per-class channel of mask_tensor, iterating channels 0..C-1 in class_order order and skipping all-zero channels (exporters/__init__.py:128-136). In that mode touching or overlapping objects of the same class MERGE into one box, and object order becomes ascending-class-id order. Two different orderings and two different box sets from the same annotations - the rewrite must keep both branches.

Boxes are measured AFTER crop and pixel priority. Each segment's mask is ANDed with the final tensor channel (segment_manager.py:297-299) and the crop zeroes pixels outside the crop rectangle while keeping full-image coordinates (file_manager.py:712-739). A crop can shrink a box, split one segment into several objects, or remove it entirely - but coordinates stay relative to the FULL image, never the crop.

No objects -> return None, no file written, an existing img.xml is NOT deleted (pascal_voc.py:52-53; exporters/__init__.py:189-206). A stale VOC file therefore survives a save that produced nothing, and will be read back later if it is first in _LOAD_CHAIN.

A class with no alias is named by its id as text, e.g. <name>2</name> (segment_manager.py:397-399). On import that numeric name is parsed back to the same integer id (file_manager.py:365-368), so UNALIASED classes are the only ones whose id survives a round trip.

An ALIASED class loses its id on the normal navigation path. SegmentManager.clear() wipes class_aliases (segment_manager.py:20-26) before the file is read (file_navigation_manager.py:281; main_window.py:2141), so _build_label_map assigns the lowest free id. Exported class 2 alias 'dog' reloads as class_id 0 with alias {0: 'dog'} - VERIFIED by running the legacy code. Do NOT write a contract test asserting class_id 2 on reload.

Two class ids sharing the same alias string MERGE into one class on reload: _build_label_map keys on the label text (file_manager.py:346,356-358). Aliases are not validated for uniqueness (segment_table_manager.py:88-93 calls set_class_alias unguarded).

An EMPTY alias string serializes as the short form <name /> (ElementTree writes ' />' when text is falsy - verified). On reload name_el.text is None, so 'name_el.text or "0"' makes the label the string '0' (file_manager.py:482), which claims class id 0 and can merge with a real class 0.

Import skip vs drop are different failures. An object with NO <name> element or NO <bndbox> element is SKIPPED before parsing (file_manager.py:474-477). An object with a present-but-empty <xmin/> gives findtext() == '' -> float('') raises ValueError -> that object is skipped (file_manager.py:483-490). An object with a MISSING <xmax> or <ymax> defaults to '0', survives parsing, then collapses and is DROPPED at the clamp check (file_manager.py:397-398) - but it has already claimed a class id. A missing <xmin>/<ymin> defaults to 0, i.e. the box is extended to the image edge rather than dropped.

'nan' as a coordinate raises ValueError from round() and is caught, skipping just that object. 'inf', '1e400' or any overflowing literal raises OverflowError, which the except (ValueError, TypeError) at file_manager.py:489 does NOT catch: it escapes load_pascal_voc_xml, is caught by the blanket handler in load_existing_mask (file_manager.py:202-204), which logs the failure and CONTINUES to the next format in the chain. One bad coordinate therefore discards the ENTIRE XML (zero segments) and silently falls through to _createml.json or .txt. Verified: float('1e400') == inf and round(inf) raises OverflowError.

Fractional coordinates written by other tools go through Python's round(), which is banker's rounding - halves go to the nearest EVEN integer: 100.5 -> 100 but 101.5 -> 102 (verified). JavaScript's Math.round() rounds halves UP and will disagree on every .5. A TypeScript port must implement round-half-to-even explicitly.
Boxes are clamped to the image: x1,y1 = max(0, .) and x2,y2 = min(w, .), min(h, .) (file_manager.py:395-396). Verified: a box (-5, -5, 9999, 9999) on a 100x100 image loads as the full image.

Interop with standard Pascal VOC tooling is BROKEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS and is preserved deliberately. The devkit convention is 1-based with an INCLUSIVE max; LazyLabel is 0-based with an EXCLUSIVE max. For the worked example the devkit would write xmin=101, xmax=110; LazyLabel writes xmin=100, xmax=110. A standard consumer computing width as xmax-xmin+1 gets 11 instead of 10 - the box reads one pixel too wide and too tall, with the extra pixel on the LEFT and TOP edges (the max edges happen to coincide). Conversely a genuine devkit file loaded into LazyLabel fills cols xmin..xmax-1, losing the right-most column and bottom row and sitting one pixel left and up of where it was meant to be.
answer: OPEN QUESTION, ANSWERED: Pascal VOC exports do NOT have to interoperate with standard VOC tooling. Per the approved decisions the rewrite reproduces legacy exports byte-identically, so the legacy convention is preserved and recorded, not fixed; legacy per-image class ids and aliases are kept as-is. Stated plainly, the legacy convention is: coordinates are 0-BASED, xmin/ymin are INCLUSIVE and xmax/ymax are EXCLUSIVE, so xmax-xmin is the pixel width (pascal_voc.py:46-49, whose docstring says so at pascal_voc.py:18-19, and the loader agrees at file_manager.py:459-460 and 400-401). The standard devkit is 1-based with an inclusive max. A consumer of these files should therefore read them as half-open 0-based pixel ranges [xmin, xmax) x [ymin, ymax); if it applies the devkit rule instead it will read every box one pixel too wide and too tall, with the extra pixel on the left and top edges, and if it FEEDS a real devkit file back to LazyLabel the box will lose its right-most column and bottom row. Both directions are accepted, documented deviations. WHAT THE CARD GOT WRONG: (1) 'parameters' listed only depth, the coordinate convention and the suffix - pose='Unspecified', truncated='0' and difficult='0' are equally hard-coded (pascal_voc.py:41-43), and the byte-identical mandate adds a whole class of serialization constants the card never mentioned: two-space ET.indent, the single-quoted <?xml version='1.0' encoding='utf-8'?> declaration, platform newline (CRLF on Windows) and NO trailing newline (pascal_voc.py:57-59, verified by running the exporter). (2) The 'then' omitted the <filename> element, which IS written and holds the bare basename (pascal_voc.py:26). (3) 'and' was null; the empty-export behaviour (no file written, existing .xml not deleted - pascal_voc.py:52-53, exporters/__init__.py:189-206) and the import-side contract belong there, because the writer and reader are one convention. (4) The edge case 'Most VOC consumers read xmax as inclusive, so boxes appear 1 px larger' is half right and imprecise about where the pixel lands - the max values coincide with the devkit's, the discrepancy is entirely at the min edge. (5) 'Class ids are not preserved when aliases exist' understates it: aliased class ids are NEVER preserved on the normal navigation path, because SegmentManager.clear() wipes class_aliases (segment_manager.py:20-26) from file_navigation_manager.py:281 and main_window.py:2141 before the XML is read, so _build_label_map hands 'dog' the lowest free id - I ran the legacy code and class 2 alias 'dog' came back as class_id 0 with class_aliases {0: 'dog'}. (6) The card's Given ('object pixels x 100-109, y 50-59') only produces one <object> if those pixels are CONNECTED; export is one object per external contour, not per segment (pascal_voc.py:35, exporters/__init__.py:114-136). WHAT AN IMPLEMENTER MUST WATCH FOR: image_size is (height, width) and is unpacked 'h, w' (pascal_voc.py:23; save_export_manager.py:397,421); 'channel' is the index into the sorted class_order, not a class id (segment_manager.py:276,283); cv2.boundingRect's w/h include both edge pixels, so xmax = x + bw already yields the exclusive bound; the loader's int(round(float(...))) is banker's rounding, which JavaScript's Math.round does not reproduce (file_manager.py:483-486); a missing <name> or <bndbox> skips the object (file_manager.py:474-477) while a missing <xmax> silently drops it AFTER it has already claimed a class id (file_manager.py:392,397-398); and an 'inf' coordinate raises OverflowError past the except at file_manager.py:489, so load_existing_mask (file_manager.py:202-204) discards the whole XML and falls through to the next format. Finally, the comment at tests/unit/core/exporters/test_exporters.py:469 calling VOC 'write-only (no loader)' is STALE - LOADABLE_FORMATS at test_exporters.py:114-122 and file_manager.py:456 both show a loader exists. Do not use that comment to justify skipping the import half of this contract.

unresolved: Nothing blocks the implementer. Two items are product-owner calls only if scope ever widens beyond byte-identical reproduction: (a) whether the rewrite should surface any warning when it IMPORTS a third-party Pascal VOC file, which the legacy code accepts silently and misreads by one pixel - byte-identical fidelity implies staying silent, so the default is 'no warning'; (b) whether user-facing documentation should state that LazyLabel .xml files are 0-based half-open and not devkit-compatible. Both are additive and neither changes the contract above.
